## Problem 6

Monotonicity is violated and sample has compliers and defiers. pi_c is proportion of subjects compliers pi_d is proportion defiers

show CACE is still identified if ATE among defiers is ATE among compliers and the proportions are not equal

Monotonicity means pi_d is not 0

$$
ITT = ATE|Complier * \pi_C - ATE|Defier * \pi_D
$$ ATE\|Compliers = ATE\|Defiers, so $ITT = (ATE|Complier$ (or) $Defier)*(\pi_C-\pi_D)$ .

Defiers means the ITT_D is the proportion of compliers net the proportion of defiers, so:

$$
CACE = \frac{ITT_Y}{ITT_D} = \frac{(ATE|CorD)*(\pi_C - \pi_D)}{\pi_C - \pi_D}
\\
CACE = ATE|CorD
$$

## Problem 8
(Pretending this extremely problematic experiment is not real)

### a
Noninterference assumes that the outcomes of one household (calls to a hotline and later arrest) are only dependent on whether the police issued a warning or arrested the accused. 

This does not seem plausible in a context (anywhere in the US, Milwaukee very much included) where crime, poverty, and policing/coercion are raced and classed. 

Moreover, I cannot imagine that police would arrest (whether holding overnight or limited time) or only issue a warrant only based on instructions from a researcher. Rather, it seems wholly probable that a frustrated or badly (un)trained cop would escalate and arrest someone in part because they had left someone else off with a ticket. So no -- I do not see how noninterference is possible. 

Excludability assumes that outcomes are affected by the treatment. A cop who is "assigned to arrest" may very well behave far more aggressively, detain someone for longer regardless of circumstances (for example -- the accused misses hourly wages, or is in precarious employment where absence/lateness has consequences, or on probation/parole so arrest means re-sentencing/re-incarceration). The well-studied collateral consequences of this terrible experiment mean there is no reason to think that future outcomes are conditional on treatment alone.

There will absolutely be police who do the opposite of what they were instructed to do. Not all cops, (!) but undoubtedly many are inured to being in positions of power, and getting told what to do by some ivory tower academics who do not understand it seems much of anything about their subject seems a sure trigger for little acts of rebellion.

### b

Always takers show up in the control group, and randomization lets us assume that pi_alwaystakers(d=0) = pi_alwaystakers(d=1)

```{r}

ITT_D <- (789/802)-(2/398)

ITT_calls <- (597/802)-(261/398)

CACE_calls <- ITT/ITT_D

itt_arrests <- 303/802 - 151/398

cace_arrests <- itt_c/ITT_D

ITT_D
ITT_calls
CACE_calls
itt_arrests
cace_arrests

```
The compliance rate is nearly 1, so the ITT for calls and CACE are similar -- assignment to treatment and treatment receipt are associated with an increase in the outcome (911 calls) of 8.9 and 9.0 respectively.

An initial arrest rather than warning is associated with a lower likeyhood of later arrest for compliers. 

### c --CHECK
Not assuming monotonicity means we throw back in the possibility of defiers (d(z=1) = 0, d(z=0)=1)) so the ITTD is not just the proportion of compliers - 0 (by assumption). Each observed treatment status group has mix of possible compliance types.

We can find bounds for never takers. The upper bound for never-takers occurs when defiers = 0.A

Among those (calls/cases) assigned to arrest who were not actually arrested, either they're never-takers or defiers, so the proportion of never takers plus the proportion of defiers is:

4/802

If there are no defiers and all are never-takers, their max possible proportion is 4/802. But if the proportion instead is only defiers and no never takers, then the proportion of never takers is 0. So the proportion of never takers is bounded by 0 and 4/802. 

Indivviduals assigned to a warning who were arrested could either be always-takers or defiers:
the sum of the proportion of always takers and of defiers is 2/398. This is the max possible proportion of always takers, and the min (0 in this proportion) is 4/802. 

Always takers are greater or equal to just over 0 (2/398-4/802), less than or equal to 2/398.  

Proportion compliers plus proportion never takers = 396/398. 

lower bound for compliers if NT = 4/802 (max)

396/398 - 4/802 < Proportion compliers < 396/398. 

UB for ATs if defiers = 0
2/398

LB for ATs if defiers are above (max)

2/398 - 4/802

Substantively, it looks like around 99% of subjects are compliers, and 0.905% are defiers. 
So removing the monot. assumption leads to an increase in assumed proportion of defiers and compliers.
